Fill in the blank.

The recent breakthroughs in CRISPR-Cas9 technology have moved the prospect of human genetic enhancement from the realm of science fiction into the laboratory. As researchers refine the precision of these “molecular scissors,” the medical community finds itself at a (A)____ While the primary goal of such technology is to eradicate hereditary diseases, the potential for non-therapeutic modifications, such as altering physical traits or cognitive abilities, has (B)____ a global debate. If these tools are to be used ethically, international regulatory bodies must first establish a consensus on where “healing” ends and “enhancement” (C)____

Notwithstanding the immense therapeutic potential, many bioethicists remain wary of the long-term consequences. The human genome is a delicately balanced system, and there is a significant risk of “off-target” effects, where unintended parts of the DNA are altered. Such errors could result in new, unforeseen health complications that (D)____ not manifest until years later. Consequently, clinical trials are being conducted under rigorous oversight, ensuring that every procedure is subjected (E)____ the highest safety standards before it can be approved for widespread use.
